business: MyLiquid Gate (runtime controls for AI agents at brokers, crypto venues and neobanks)
why_not: I won't put an inline proxy from a startup with no customers and no SOC 2 report in front of our order path, even for free. If it goes down or gets breached, our trades stop and I'm the one explaining it to FINRA.

I won't put a startup without a SOC 2 report in our order path, and this one has no customers and only a planned audit. Nothing in writing from FINRA or the SEC makes me need agent-level pre-trade controls yet, so it's not going into next year's budget.

Our agent volume through the MCP server is tiny today, and no regulator has written a rule or brought an enforcement action that says I need a separate agent-identity and approval layer. I'm not putting a proxy in front of customer trades, or signing a letter of intent with a price in it, on the strength of speeches and reports.

I like being first, but our agent volume is tiny today and my engineers already rate-limit every API key, so there's nothing here I'd pay for this month. At our volume we'd sit inside the free tier anyway, and I won't sign an LOI naming a price for a problem we don't have at scale yet.

My team already rate-limits every key and could build caps, an approval queue and a kill switch for agent accounts inside a quarter, and no regulator is asking me for this yet. I don't buy what I can build, especially not something that sits in my order path.

Our agent volume is tiny today, and a proxy that checks caps, routes big orders to a human and has a kill switch is something my team can build in a quarter on top of controls we already run. I'll answer the examiner's AI question with our own policy and logs, not a vendor with no customers sitting in the trade path.

Identity check, per-customer caps, a human-approval queue and a kill switch in front of our own order path is a quarter of work for my team, and with a competitor already live we'd rather own that layer than rent it. I'd take the demo call to steal the checklist, not to sign.

A policy check in front of our MCP server, an approval queue, a kill switch and a hash-chained log are things my team can build in a quarter, and we'd rather own anything that sits in the trade path. I'm not putting a startup with no customers and no SOC 2 in front of order execution, and I'm not signing an LOI with a price on it just to get six free months.

I'm building next year's budget right now and this isn't in it. A metered tool from a startup with no customers loses to a headcount line every time. At most I'd let my engineers poke at the free Developer tier. That isn't buying.
why_yes: We opened our MCP server to customers' agents this year, and I have nothing between an agent's call and an executed trade except our own caps, so I'd take the free design-partner slot and run it in shadow mode on a slice of traffic. That's a pilot, not a budget line yet. Whether we pay comes down to what the six months show.

We're letting customer agents onto the venue and right now our controls are rate limits plus hope, so I'd take the free design-partner slot and run it in shadow mode next to the order path. I'd sign the LOI only if the price has a ceiling. Paying the Growth tier comes after it proves itself, and it goes into next year's budget as a line item conditional on the pilot.

A competitor announced agent trading last month, and a free six-month pilot with no code change gets us a governed answer in weeks instead of the quarters my own team would need. I'd sign up as a design partner in a sandbox, but that's a pilot, not a production commitment.
